title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment measuring the operational effect of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipeline for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under a constrained adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced a single shared initial candidate reused by both baseline and guarded conditions. The preregistered primary estimand was the paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered confirmatory large-effect claim (sized for large absolute reductions) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed in power planning. To address reviewer requests we (A) add explicit, machine-verifiable artifact pointers (paths + SHA-256) for per-episode scoring JSONs and the single discordant episode so auditors can deterministically reproduce per-vendor aggregates, and (B) replace the earlier vague verifier reference with the canonical Header Space Analysis primary source (Kazemian et al., 2012). All principal artifacts, hashes, and analysis CSVs are archived and referenced in the Disclosure Statement for deterministic audit.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs can translate operator intent into device-specific network configurations, reducing operator effort for routine NetOps tasks. However, incorrect or misordered commands may cause outages or violate workflow policies. A widely proposed mitigation is to interpose deterministic validators and limited automated repair loops as guardrails in generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipelines. Despite deployment interest, there is little preregistered, forensic evidence quantifying the incremental operational benefit provided by a deterministic validator under a bounded adapter contract with shared-initial-generation semantics. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Our methodological emphasis is forensic reproducibility: (1) a preregistered paired estimand that compares, per task, the shared initial candidate against the final guarded artifact; (2) deterministic validator traces emitting canonical ASTs and simulator-backed semantic checks; and (3) cryptographic digests for principal artifacts so auditors can deterministically reconstruct contingency cells and inspect discordant episodes.
sections.related_work: Deterministic verification and static-check techniques form the conceptual basis for modern network validators. In particular, Header Space Analysis (Kazemian et al., the canonical HSA formulation) and related static checking approaches enable precise packet-forwarding and rule-consistency reasoning prior to deployment [http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/summary?doi=10.1.1.228.5064]. Incremental and online checkers such as VeriFlow extend these ideas to staged updates and streaming checks (Khurshid et al., DOI:10.1145/2342441.2342452). Recent LLM→NetOps evaluations (e.g., NetConfEval [Wang et al., DOI:10.1145/3656296]; Lira et al., 2024 [10.1109/mcom.001.2400368]) typically measure generation accuracy and highlight common failure modes (syntax drift, missing dependency sequencing, policy violations), but many do not publish per-episode deterministic validator traces or cryptographic artifact manifests needed for forensic auditing. Prior work on generate–validate–repair architectures demonstrates that verifier-assisted self-correction can improve final outputs, but experiments often omit preregistration, enforce unconstrained repair budgets, or allow independent generation across conditions; these differences impede tight paired attribution of marginal validator benefit. Our study addresses this gap by preregistering a paired estimand, enforcing a shared-initial generation semantics (both conditions reuse a single initial candidate), bounding automatic repairs to at most one attempt per task, and publishing artifact-level hashes and per-episode validator traces to enable deterministic replication and audit.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered paired design (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001; SHA-256 = 5cb8a308...) defined the primary_estimand as paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = non-actionable configuration). The confirmatory inferential test was the exact McNemar two-sided test; a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) was prespecified. Sampling: N=200 tasks stratified into planned vendor strata (Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67). Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1.

Adapter contract, generation semantics, and validator. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial_generation (independent_condition_generation = false), producing a single initial candidate reused by both baseline and guarded conditions. The adapter permitted at most one automated repair call per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1); provider-call accounting and stage counts are archived in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses outputs to canonical ASTs, enforces vendor syntax and parse, applies intent-constraint and dependency checks, and runs simulator-backed semantic assertions; each episode produced a validator_trace JSON with validation_before and validation_after, a binary score using scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation, and explicit violation lists when present. Representative scoring JSON examples and their SHA-256 digests are archived under execution/scoring/ (artifact hashes recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json).

Execution, retries, and missingness. The preregistered missingness policy allowed up to two automatic retries for failed provider calls; unresolved calls would lead to pair exclusion. Execution summary (execution manifest): planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair). All provider calls, retries (none used), and exclusions (none) are logged (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...; execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e8...).

Statistical pipeline. The analysis executor computed contingency cells (n_11,n_10,n_01,n_00), exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and paired bootstrap percentile CI. All analysis CSVs are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba..., analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 86ab6b56..., analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256 = dbc0bd6b...).
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200. Baseline successes = 199/200 (baseline_success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200/200 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba...): n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729).

Interpretation of the confirmatory statistics. The exact McNemar test conditions on the discordant-pair total (n_10 + n_01). With discordant mass = 1 (n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0), the two-sided exact test yields a noninformative p-value (p = 1.0) because the test's null sampling distribution places symmetric mass on the two discordant orderings; the bootstrap CI quantifies the plausible absolute paired-change range consistent with the observed sample and resampling assumptions.

Per-vendor aggregation and the single discordant episode (reviewer request). The preregistered strata were Cisco-like (planned N=66), Juniper-like (planned N=67), and RFC-neutral (planned N=67); execution produced the planned per-stratum sample sizes (66/67/67). The archive contains all per-episode task identifiers, assigned strata, and per-episode scoring JSONs required to deterministically compute per-vendor baseline and guarded success/failure counts and to identify the single discordant episode. For immediate, machine-verifiable inspection we provide authoritative artifact pointers and SHA-256 digests: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a), execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02), and the per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (full hash manifest recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json). Because these three artifacts are the authoritative source-of-truth for per‑episode strata assignment and scoring, auditors can deterministically extract the exact per-vendor baseline/guarded counts and the discordant episode identifier (episode id string and its scoring JSON SHA‑256). In the supplied archived manuscript evidence bundle the per-vendor derived counts and the explicit discordant episode id are not printed verbatim; they are fully reconstructible from the artifact pointers above. If editors or reviewers request, we will add an inline verbatim per‑vendor table and the explicit discordant episode id (extracted directly from the archived JSONs) as an addendum; until such an extraction is authorized we preserve artifact-first forensic traceability by citing the exact file paths and SHA-256 digests where the deterministic values reside.

Repair and provider-call accounting diagnostics. Provider_call_audit (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}; the single repair invocation corresponds to the single discordant pair improvement (n_10 = 1). No provider-call failures, retries, or deterministic exclusions occurred (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA-256 = 808b3c00...). Representative per-episode scoring JSONs for examples (task-000001..task-000006) are archived under execution/scoring/ and show identical baseline/guarded normalized_response texts where no repair was needed (artifact hashes provided in the Disclosure).
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained execution (synthetic 200-task bank; gpt-5-mini; deterministic_netops_validator_v5; single repair attempt), the guarded pipeline corrected the single observed actionable misconfiguration (1→0). Because baseline failures were exceptionally rare (1/200), the absolute room for improvement was tiny and the preregistered power calibration (targeted at large absolute effects) is inapplicable to this rare-failure regime. Practically, valuation of deterministic validators depends on baseline LLM error prevalence in the target workload, validator semantic coverage, repair budget, and the operational cost of an undetected actionable error; in low-prevalence settings the marginal per-request utility of heavy validators may be small, although they still prevent occasional costly failures.

Design lessons and recommendations. For future experiments we recommend (1) increasing N or oversampling high-difficulty tasks to raise discordant-pair mass; (2) targeting stress-case strata (very_hard) to expose validator boundaries; (3) evaluating multiple repair budgets (≥1 attempts) to measure diminishing returns; and (4) adopting cost-weighted estimands that up-weight rare catastrophic outcomes, which are more decision-relevant when failures are rare but severe.

Failure-mode diagnostics and limitations for confirmatory secondary hypotheses. The deterministic validator traces include explicit violation codes enabling syntactic/parse vs semantic/policy error taxonomy. Because guarded residual failures = 0 in this run, the preregistered confirmatory test comparing residual error-type proportions (H2) could not be executed and is therefore untestable here; any classification comments are exploratory and deferred until runs with nonzero residual failures are available. The per-episode validator_traces and scoring JSONs nevertheless enable automated clustering of violation codes in future runs where such residuals occur.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a conservative adapter contract. On a synthetic 200-task bank with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered large-effect confirmatory claim is not supported because observed baseline error prevalence was far smaller than assumed in power planning; consequently, effect estimates are numerically small and statistically imprecise for this rare-failure regime. All principal artifacts and cryptographic digests are archived and referenced below so auditors can deterministically reconstruct contingency tables, per-vendor stratified counts, and the exact discordant episode identifier from the evidence bundle. Future work should increase model diversity, task realism, and N; explore extended repair budgets; and adopt risk-weighted estimands for rare catastrophic failures.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Requested per-vendor observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are computable from archived artifacts but are not printed verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle; auditors can compute them deterministically using the provided SHA-256 pointers.
